body:
So to be clear, this does not happen without the `new Image().src` assignment? That does seem strangely side-effecting.

cc @rwlbuis @nt1m

I have not debugged, but from a quick code inspection I suspect what happens is that the lazy load gets registered in the WebKit cached resources subsystem, and once the cached resource load finishes it causes notifications to all load observers, including the lazy load image.

So I think this is a side-effect of the WebKit cached resources subsystem. I do not know though if it is crucial to register lazy loads in the webkit cached resources subsystem, but I would not be surprised if things break without that.

I'd be curious to hear from Blink folks if they made a conscious decision about this and if they have same behaviour as WebKit because of a similar cached resources subsystem.

> So to be clear, this does not happen without the new Image().src assignment? That does seem strangely side-effecting.

Correct, and agreed.

Chrome and Safari actually do agree with Firefox on [the testcase](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/attachment.cgi?id=9428769) under one condition: if I open the browser's network-DevTools panel and check the "Disable Caches" checkbox.  (Under that configuration, Chrome and Safari render the testcase as blank.)

The fact that this checkbox gives different behavior vs. the "cache-skipping reload" (Shift+Reload) in those browsers seems unexpected/unwanted.
Chrome and Safari have even worse bugs here, see: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/375209498
@domfarolino, back in the day you used to work on lazy-loading images---would you be able to help with a Chromium and/or spec perspective here?

FWIW I wrote a test for this: https://wpt.fyi/results/html/semantics/embedded-content/the-img-element/update-the-image-data/lazy-out-of-band-load.html

Extra Safari issue: https://wpt.fyi/results/html/semantics/embedded-content/the-img-element/update-the-image-data/src-then-lazy-load.html
FYI, I'm investigating this, and I think there's a simple [fix](https://issues.chromium.org/u/2/issues/375209498#comment6) for chromium.

Digging a bit further, I came across an interesting [test](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html/semantics/embedded-content/the-img-element/image-loading-lazy-use-list-of-available-images.html). This seems to muddy the issue: if an image resource has already been loaded via other means by the time 'loading="lazy"' is applied to an `` it will load (and fire its load event) immediately; but if the image resource completes loading at a later time, then the lazy-loading behavior persists and it doesn't fire its load event right away. This is pretty quirky, and I also wonder if it could be the basis of a timing attack. @emilio WDYT?
That is what the spec says to do (the list of available images stuff is checked before entering the lazy load state).
@emilio Should we consider an update to the spec, or does this behavior seem OK to you?

Seems ok to me at a glance, it's consistent with how `src` loads synchronously if already in the available image list, and it prevents flickering when mutating the DOM? I added tests for that behavior in [Mozilla bug 1709577](https://bugzil.la/1709577).

I think this also looks right to me. This is very related to my comment above https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10671#issuecomment-2450198052, where I mention Chromium's quirks wrt the list of available image "matching", and where we make the decision to lazy load.

I filed a WebKit bug: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=303993

Closing since it seems the spec should stay as-is.

Firefox's behavior has resulted in a web compat issue: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2011480

Do we still want to keep the spec as-is? (I think it would be ideal since IMO it makes more sense, but Chromium and WebKit would need to align with Gecko/spec.)
It seems only WebKit is still failing the tests @emilio added? Is there a missing test if you're suggesting Chromium still needs to align?

I see in https://issues.chromium.org/issues/375209498 that some patches have landed so the tests in https://wpt.fyi/results/html/semantics/embedded-content/the-img-element/update-the-image-data/lazy-out-of-band-load.html now pass.

In https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2016233#c15 @EdgarChen found a similar case which still loads 2 images in Chromium (1 in Gecko and WebKit). I can convert this test to wpt.

> It seems only WebKit is still failing the tests [@emilio](https://github.com/emilio) added? Is there a missing test if you're suggesting Chromium still needs to align?

Yes. `lazy-out-of-band-load.html` only asserts that no `load` or `error` event fires. Chromium passes it now but still gives the deferred image its real `naturalWidth`/`naturalHeight` and `currentSrc`, with `complete` false and no events fired.

I wrote a test for that part: `lazy-out-of-band-load-no-image-data.html`, landing in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2063806. Same setup as the existing test, but it asserts `complete === false` and `naturalWidth === 0` after the out of band load. It covers `src` and `srcset`, each with `display:none` and below-viewport.

Gecko: 4/4 pass.
Chromium: 4/4 fail, `lazy image has no natural width expected 0 but got 100`.
WebKit: 4/4 fail earlier, on `load: should never try to load`.

Another site broke on this in the meantime: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2062220. It only needs the dimensions, not the events, so Chromium's event fix doesn't help it.

Two (maybe dumb) questions about the test in https://bug2016233.bmoattachments.org/attachment.cgi?id=9548391:
 1. Because `img2` is visible and in the viewport, it having `loading=lazy` is immaterial, right? Since it loads fine, it inserts the image into the list of available images for later re-use.
 2. Per spec, doesn't setting the _invisible_ `img.src = ""` correctly re-invoke "updating the image data" for `img`, which selects the cached source from the list of available images, thus correctly bypassing its `loading=lazy`? (Since the list of available images is consulted before the image element's loading state is).

When an image is loaded from the list of available image, its image data is "completely available", which I think would make `.complete` return true, and give it real natural dimensions, no?

> Two (maybe dumb) questions about the test in https://bug2016233.bmoattachments.org/attachment.cgi?id=9548391:
> 
>     1. Because `img2` is visible and in the viewport, it having `loading=lazy` is immaterial, right? Since it loads fine, it inserts the image into the list of available images for later re-use.

Correct.

>     2. Per spec, doesn't setting the _invisible_ `img.src = ""` correctly re-invoke "updating the image data" for `img`, which selects the cached source from the list of available images, thus correctly bypassing its `loading=lazy`? (Since the list of available images is consulted before the image element's loading state is).

We never hit the list of available images in this case. Note that the only place that the list of available images is consulted is in step 7. Step 4 says "Let selected source be null...". Step 5 "If the element does not use srcset or picture..", so step 5 does not apply. Step 6 doesn't touch selected source. And then all of step 7 is conditional on "If selected source is not null".

I think we should keep the spec as-is. Other lazy-loading elements don't do this. A lazy `iframe` stays deferred after another iframe or `fetch()` loads the same URL (Chromium, Gecko, WebKit). A lazy `video`'s media and poster stay deferred too (in Chromium, the only engine with `loading` on `video` currently). That includes the poster when an `img` in the same document has loaded its URL. That seems right for `iframe` and `video`, and I think it's reasonable to make `img` consistent.
